summary: The lecture explores security architectures, contrasting traditional access control with the Zero Trust Architecture, emphasizing principles like least privilege and micro-segmentation. It delves into advanced security techniques such as behavioral analytics, privacy-preserving methods (differential privacy, zero-knowledge proofs), and common vulnerabilities (CVEs). Finally, it examines historical security improvements in Android and highlights the foundational challenge of trust in system design through Ken Thompson's "Trusting Trust" attack.
title: Operating System Security: Architectures, Vulnerabilities, and Trust

fun_fact_idea.exciting_angle: Connect Zero Trust Architecture and micro-segmentation to how major cloud platforms (like AWS, Azure, GCP) achieve robust isolation for multi-tenant applications. This demonstrates how low-level security principles are critical for building scalable and secure cloud products, directly relevant to an aspiring Software Engineer.
